subject: SummitCorp private hosting: audit cadence, custody and pricing ask
messages:
From: Dana Morris <dana.morris@summitcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@summitcorp.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting + audit window / custody ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. SummitCorp is excited about the Private offering. Two items we need to lock before procurement can finalize:

1) Audit cadence and scope — legal wants a quarterly audit right for the next 24 months (covers on-prem nodes and audit logs). Can you confirm Redwood will accept quarterly audits by our third-party auditor and provide the log retention/export format?

2) Data custody/egress — for regulatory reasons we need a 30-day hold on any outbound egress to any non-Summit systems. We understand this is a deviation; this will be reflected in contract language and we are open to a fee for the operational burden.

3) Pricing — if we commit to a 36-month reserved capacity contract and accept a 120-day notice for terminations, SummitCorp is requesting a 30% platform discount vs list.

I'm attaching our preliminary SOW and a high level dataflow diagram. Can you route this to deal desk and legal? Procurement would like an answer by COB next Wednesday (Aug 4).

Thanks,
Dana Morris
Head of Cloud Ops
SummitCorp
Attachments: SummitCorp-SOW-draft.pdf (application/pdf), DataFlow-Diagram.png (image/png)

Dana — really appreciate the clarity and the SOW. I’m looping in Marissa (deal desk) and Lauren (legal) to review the asks. Short answer: we can likely support a modified audit cadence and a restricted egress window, but both require legal sign-off and an ops-runbook. The 30% off list for 36 months is material; I’ll let Marissa weigh in on the discount band.

I’ll push for a response by Aug 4 but want to set expectations that any approval will be conditional on a small fee for custodial tooling and a scoped audit template (to limit operational disruption).

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm deal desk appetite and pricing levers? Lauren — can legal propose redline language for quarterly audits and the egress hold?

Cheers,
Ben Carter

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private hosting + audit window / custody ask

Ben — thanks for the heads up. Quick notes from deal desk:

- Discount: SummitCorp’s requested 30% exceeds our standard max for 36-month commit. Deal desk can approve up to 20% with standard concessions (non-refundable set-up fee, minimum quarterly billing). Anything >20% requires exec signoff (Rishi).
- Audit cadence: Quarterly audits are operationally heavy. We have precedent for annual audits with an expanded scope + one remote/one on-site in year 1. If SummitCorp insists on quarterly, we should limit to remote/SC logging review only and cap on-site to once per year.
- Egress hold: A 30-day outbound egress hold is non-standard. We can offer a 14-day quarantine for outbound integrations with an additional operations fee (monthly). A full 30-day legal covenant that prevents Redwood-initiated egress will need an indemnity clause and likely a higher fee.

I’ve attached a proposed SOW redline (see attachment) with pricing tiers and suggested audit guardrails. Recommend we surface the >20% discount and full 30-day custody ask to Rishi for exec approval.

Attachments: DealDesk-Summit-sow-redline.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Deal Desk Manager

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting + audit window / custody ask

Ben / Marissa — 

I reviewed SummitCorp’s SOW and the proposed audit/egress language. Key legal points:

1) Quarterly audits by a third-party: acceptable if we define scope narrowly (log review, access controls, configuration — no live forensic triage) and require 14 days notice. We should restrict auditors to a vetted list or require use of our approved audit partner to avoid operational risk.

2) 30-day egress hold: problematic. If SummitCorp requires a contractual prohibition on Redwood-initiated egress for 30 days, we need: (a) an explicit indemnity for any regulatory fines resulting from retained data, (b) a defined exception process for emergency obligations (e.g., legal holds), and (c) a one-time operational onboarding fee plus monthly custody fee.

3) Redlines: I’ve drafted proposed clauses and will circulate a tracked PDF. If Deal Desk needs a shortcut, we can offer a concession: 20% discount + 14-day egress hold + documented audit scope (quarterly remote log reviews + annual on-site) — anything beyond requires exec approval (pricing or legal carveout).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Aug 03, 2026 at 09:26 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Lauren — Marissa, can you confirm whether SummitCorp prefers the 20% + 14-day hold path or pushing for 30% + 30-day custody? Procurement needs clear position.

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting + audit window / custody ask

Folks — I reviewed the background and the numbers. I’m comfortable approving a two-path offer to SummitCorp:

1) Standard concession path (auto-approve by deal desk): 36-month reserved commitment at 20% off list, 14-day egress hold, quarterly remote log reviews, one annual on-site audit. Standard onboarding fee applies.

2) Executive concession (requires this email as approval + subsequent SOW language): 36-month reserved commitment at 30% off list, 30-day egress hold, quarterly remote audits with one additional limited on-site (i.e., two site visits in year 1), and a one-time custody operations fee of $95,000 plus a $9,500/month custody maintenance charge.

Conditions for the exec concession: SummitCorp signs the redlined SLA (limits auditor scope to logging and configuration reviews), agrees to add Redwood as an indemnitee for fines arising from retained customer data beyond normal retention, and accepts a 120-day no-termination window. Offer expires COB Aug 10.

I’m authorizing this on the condition that Legal finalizes redlines and Finance signs off on the $95k setup fee/cost waterfall. Marissa — please prepare an approval memo and countersigned SOW template for the customer.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales Operations
